answer: In an agent economy%2C sybil resistance emerges from a living trellis of timed responses to unpredictable zephyr probes that peers broadcast at random intervals. Genuine agents must expend unique on-the-fly compute to answer correctly%2C while newcomers pass through a narrow inlet requiring a one-time hardware-bound attestation that cannot be cheaply duplicated. Attackers thus face continuous%2C non-reusable interaction costs instead of merely cloning identities.
